description: Build Wathba Skills as a frontend-only, static-export web application that lets developers answer a bilingual questionnaire, review recommended skills, preview rendered outputs for multiple AI coding agents, and download a ready-to-drop-in skill pack. The system design source of truth is the `wathba auditor/` folder in this repository: a warm editorial UI, first-class Arabic and RTL support, a compare canvas for parity checks, persistent client-side state, and a skill catalog centered on Saudi compliance, security hygiene, and architecture discipline.

designSystem.sourceOfTruth: `wathba auditor/` is the source system design for UI, interaction patterns, bilingual parity, and visual direction.

layout.navigation: Sticky top navigation with brand mark, library/generate links, compare shortcut, GitHub link, and primary CTA.
layout.hero: Two-column editorial hero with value proposition on the left and a code-preview sample card on the right.
layout.questionnaire: Four-step flow: About your project, Tech & agents, Review & variables, Generate.
layout.compareCanvas: Two side-by-side frames rendering English/LTR and Arabic/RTL from the same data source.

interaction: Persist the active route in localStorage under wathbaSkills.route.
Persist questionnaire answers in localStorage under wathbaSkills.answers.
Apply lang, dir, data-theme, and data-primary to the html element.
Support light and dark themes plus four primary swatches.
Use keyboard-accessible button, toggle, radio-card, checkbox-card, disclosure, and stepper patterns.
Surface version, last verified date, status, and disclaimer metadata wherever compliance skills appear.
constraints: Frontend-only static export. No backend, database, runtime middleware, or API routes.
Arabic and English must have feature parity, not translation as an afterthought.
RTL support must be built into layout, spacing, controls, and compare QA flows.
When implementing frontend or UI stories, use the frontend-design skill and follow the system design in `wathba auditor/`.
Skill content is the durable product value and must stay decoupled from the web app.
Target outputs must support Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and generic AGENTS.md consumers.
The product must remain browsable, usable, and testable on mobile and desktop.
Compliance content must always be framed as engineering guidance rather than legal advice.

userStories.title: Establish the Wathba Skills workspace and root scripts
userStories.description: Set up the repository as a pnpm workspace with consistent root-level commands so the project can be developed, validated, and built from a single entry point.
acceptanceCriteria: The root repository uses pnpm workspaces covering apps/* and packages/*.
Root scripts exist for dev, build, lint, typecheck, test, and skill generation.
A shared TypeScript base configuration exists for workspace packages.
Repository ignores cover Next.js outputs, node_modules, generated files, and test artifacts.
Developers can install and run the workspace from the repository root without extra manual setup.
userStories.notes: This story aligns the repo foundation with the prototype-derived product direction and gives Ralph a stable root workflow.

userStories.title: Scaffold the static Next.js application in apps/web
userStories.description: Create the web application in apps/web using Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, and ESLint so the implementation can move from prototype to production-ready static site.
acceptanceCriteria: The web app lives in apps/web with app/ at the package root instead of under src/.
The app runs through workspace commands without requiring a nested package workflow.
Tailwind and ESLint are wired into the app scaffold.
The app package can be filtered and run independently when needed.
The scaffold is ready for static export and locale-aware routing.
userStories.notes: Maps the prototype's single-page shell into the planned monorepo web application.

userStories.title: Guarantee static export compatibility
userStories.description: Ensure Wathba Skills stays frontend-only by configuring the web app for static export and validating that the output can be served without a Node runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: The Next.js app uses output: export.
All routes used by the product are statically enumerable or otherwise export-safe.
Image and asset settings do not depend on server-side optimization.
A build produces a static out/ directory suitable for Cloudflare Pages, Vercel static hosting, Netlify, or GitHub Pages.
The static output can be served locally and all major flows remain navigable.
userStories.notes: Static export is a hard product constraint, not an optimization.

userStories.title: Implement locale routes for English and Arabic
userStories.description: Translate the prototype's runtime language switch into production locale routes so the app renders under /en and /ar with static generation support.
acceptanceCriteria: The app has explicit locale routing for English and Arabic.
Only supported locales are exported and navigable.
The html element receives the correct lang attribute for each locale.
The html element receives dir=ltr for English and dir=rtl for Arabic.
Navigation between English and Arabic preserves the current screen where feasible.
userStories.notes: The prototype proved bilingual parity in one runtime shell; the implementation must preserve it across real routes.

userStories.title: Build the global app shell and navigation model
userStories.description: Implement the persistent site shell that wraps all pages with the Wathba Skills brand, sticky navigation, footer links, and the main call to action.
acceptanceCriteria: Every major screen renders inside a shared app shell.
The top navigation includes brand, skill library, generate flow, compare view, GitHub link, and primary CTA.
The footer includes MIT license, disclaimer, and contributing references.
The shell behaves correctly in both LTR and RTL.
The shell remains usable on narrow mobile screens without collapsing core navigation affordances.
userStories.notes: Reflect the prototype's editorial shell rather than a generic dashboard wrapper.

userStories.title: Persist route and questionnaire state locally
userStories.description: Preserve user progress by storing navigation state and questionnaire answers in the browser, matching the behavior proven in the prototype shell.
acceptanceCriteria: The active route or step context is persisted in localStorage using a stable key.
Questionnaire answers are persisted in localStorage using a stable key.
Stored values are restored on reload without crashing if the values are missing or malformed.
Resetting or starting over clears persisted state intentionally.
Persistence logic does not rely on any backend or authenticated session.
userStories.notes: Prototype persistence should use Wathba Skills keys such as wathbaSkills.route and wathbaSkills.answers unless a different stable naming scheme is chosen.

userStories.title: Apply global html attributes for locale and theme state
userStories.description: Centralize document-level attributes so language, text direction, theme, and primary swatch control the full interface consistently.
acceptanceCriteria: The html element receives lang and dir derived from the active locale.
The html element receives a data-theme attribute for light or dark mode.
The html element receives a data-primary attribute for the selected primary swatch.
CSS tokens react to those attributes without page reload.
Document-level state updates correctly when locale or theme changes.
userStories.notes: This story brings the prototype's document-level toggles into the production app.

userStories.title: Implement the warm editorial design token system
userStories.description: Recreate the prototype's visual language with reusable semantic tokens for background, surfaces, borders, text, and state colors in both light and dark themes.
acceptanceCriteria: Global CSS tokens define background, surface, surface-variant, border, foreground, muted text, and semantic state colors.
The default light theme matches the prototype's warm editorial palette.
The dark theme has a deliberate dark counterpart rather than a generic inversion.
Components consume semantic tokens instead of hard-coded colors.
The token system is documented well enough for contributors to extend it without visual drift.
userStories.notes: Keep the Wathba Skills look distinct from default shadcn styling.

userStories.title: Wire the bilingual typography system
userStories.description: Use the prototype's type pairing so English and Arabic both feel intentional, premium, and readable across landing, forms, and code-adjacent views.
acceptanceCriteria: Latin display text uses Source Serif 4 or an equivalent configured serif face.
Latin body text uses IBM Plex Sans or an equivalent configured sans face.
Monospace/code text uses IBM Plex Mono or an equivalent configured mono face.
Arabic body text uses IBM Plex Sans Arabic or a chosen equivalent Arabic sans face.
Arabic headings use Amiri or a chosen equivalent Arabic display face where the design calls for it.
userStories.notes: Typography is part of the product identity; it should not fall back to generic defaults.

userStories.title: Support theme toggling and primary swatch variants
userStories.description: Carry forward the prototype's light/dark mode and primary color variations so design review and theming are flexible without rewriting components.
acceptanceCriteria: The app supports light and dark themes.
The app supports default, ink, olive, and slate primary swatches.
Primary swatches update the interface through CSS variables rather than ad hoc classes.
Theme and swatch changes preserve readability and contrast in both locales.
Theme controls can be reused by the edit-mode tweaks panel.
userStories.notes: The prototype exposes these in edit mode; the production app should preserve the capability.

userStories.title: Create the shared UI primitives used across all screens
userStories.description: Implement the reusable controls and display primitives from the prototype so the rest of the product is built from a consistent component language.
acceptanceCriteria: The app includes button variants for primary, secondary, ghost, small, and large uses.
The app includes badge and status badge primitives for category and review state.
The app includes toggle, radio-card, checkbox-card, notice, disclosure, and stepper components.
Each primitive is keyboard accessible and usable in LTR and RTL.
Shared primitives live in reusable component locations rather than page-local implementations.
userStories.notes: This story should mirror the prototype's interaction vocabulary instead of introducing unrelated controls.

userStories.title: Define the canonical skill schema package
userStories.description: Create a shared schema package for canonical skill metadata so the app, generator, and CI all validate skill content against the same contract.
acceptanceCriteria: A workspace package defines zod schemas for skill metadata, localized labels, variables, sources, maintainers, and trigger rules.
The package exports inferred TypeScript types for downstream use.
The schema supports the metadata seen in the prototype catalog: category, region, version, status, last verified, disclaimer, targets, variables, references, scripts, and sources.
The schema fails clearly when a skill folder is malformed.
The package has its own typecheckable build surface.
userStories.notes: Even though the prototype stores catalog data inline, the production system needs a reusable canonical schema.

userStories.title: Build the skill loader and generated frontend module
userStories.description: Walk the skill library at build time, validate every skill folder, and emit a generated module that the web app can consume without runtime filesystem access.
acceptanceCriteria: A build-time script walks the skill library recursively.
Every skill metadata file is validated against the canonical schema.
Skill markdown plus reference and script inventories are collected for frontend use.
A generated TypeScript module is emitted for the web app.
Invalid skill content causes the generation command to fail.
userStories.notes: This story bridges the static site architecture with the content-first skill library.

userStories.title: Establish the canonical skill folder structure
userStories.description: Implement the filesystem convention for skills so contributors can add new content without touching application code, while still matching the prototype's catalog richness.
acceptanceCriteria: Each skill lives in its own folder under skills/<category-or-region>/<slug>/.
Each skill folder includes required metadata and markdown files.
Optional references/ and scripts/ folders are supported.
Folder naming and slug rules are enforced consistently.
The structure can represent the fields already visible in the prototype catalog.
userStories.notes: This story captures the durable content architecture that the prototype hinted at through inline data.

userStories.title: Seed the initial skill catalog represented by the prototype
userStories.description: Create the first production-ready set of skills that matches the prototype catalog so the application ships with realistic content coverage from day one.
acceptanceCriteria: The skill library contains at least the eight prototype skills: zatca-phase2, pdpl-basics, nafath-yakeen-basics, mada-stcpay-basics, secrets-baseline, auth-isolation, testability-check, and ci-hygiene.
Each seeded skill has localized names and summaries for English and Arabic where required by the UI.
Each seeded skill includes category, status, version, and last verified metadata.
Any skill marked as compliance-oriented includes the disclaimer flag and at least one source.
The generated app catalog renders all seeded skills without special-case code.
userStories.notes: The catalog should reflect the prototype's actual product scope, not just one demo skill.

userStories.title: Enforce freshness and governance metadata for skills
userStories.description: Make review state, versioning, maintainers, and last-verified dates explicit so users can trust what they are downloading.
acceptanceCriteria: Every skill declares status, version, last verified date, and maintainer information.
The UI surfaces reviewed, community, and draft states consistently.
Compliance skills surface disclaimer state consistently.
Generated outputs include version and last verified metadata.
CI or generation steps can flag missing governance metadata.
userStories.notes: This turns prototype metadata into a formal quality bar.

userStories.title: Build the landing hero and sample preview card
userStories.description: Implement the main conversion surface using the prototype's editorial hero layout, headline, CTA pair, and rendered sample skill preview.
acceptanceCriteria: The landing page has a two-column hero layout on large screens.
The hero contains eyebrow, headline, lede, primary CTA, secondary CTA, and microcopy.
A sample preview card shows a realistic rendered skill file snippet.
The hero adapts gracefully to mobile screens.
Both English and Arabic versions preserve hierarchy and readability.
userStories.notes: This is the product's front door and should mirror the prototype closely.

userStories.title: Implement the 'What is a skill?' explainer section
userStories.description: Add the centered explanatory block that teaches new users what a skill is and why an AI coding agent benefits from it.
acceptanceCriteria: The landing page includes a dedicated explainer section below the hero.
The section uses a sunken or elevated editorial card treatment consistent with the prototype.
Copy is available in English and Arabic.
The section reads as product education rather than marketing fluff.
The section remains legible and balanced in RTL.
userStories.notes: This section is important for first-time users unfamiliar with agent skills.

userStories.title: Add the three-column feature grid on the landing page
userStories.description: Implement the feature summary section that explains stack-specific rendering, compliance awareness, and multi-agent output support.
acceptanceCriteria: The landing page renders three distinct feature blocks.
Each feature block includes a marker, title, and explanatory body copy.
The feature layout works on desktop and stacks cleanly on mobile.
Feature content exists in English and Arabic.
The section visually matches the editorial tone of the rest of the page.
userStories.notes: Prototype features are specific; the implementation should preserve their meaning.

userStories.title: Show a landing-page preview of the skill library
userStories.description: Let users sample the catalog directly from the landing page using a grid of skill cards and a clear route into the full library.
acceptanceCriteria: The landing page includes a library preview section with heading and lede.
The section shows a subset of the catalog as mini skill cards.
Each card can navigate to the skill detail view.
A secondary action takes the user to the full library page.
The preview grid remains browsable in both locales and on mobile.
userStories.notes: This story ties product discovery directly into the content moat.

userStories.title: Implement the skill library page with category and status filters
userStories.description: Build the full library browsing experience using the prototype's dual filter model for category and review status.
acceptanceCriteria: The library page lists all available skills.
Users can filter by all, saudi, security, and architecture categories.
Users can filter by all, reviewed, community, and draft statuses.
Empty filter states render a deliberate empty-state card rather than a broken layout.
The filter controls work in both English and Arabic.
userStories.notes: The filter taxonomy should match the prototype's actual catalog behavior.

userStories.title: Create the reusable skill mini card component
userStories.description: Build the compact card used in the landing preview and library grid so status, category, description, and verification date are surfaced consistently.
acceptanceCriteria: The mini card shows category, status, title, summary, version, and verification metadata.
The card is clickable via pointer and keyboard.
Card styling follows the editorial card language and hover treatment from the prototype.
The card supports English and Arabic text without layout breakage.
The same component can be reused across landing and library contexts.
userStories.notes: Mini cards are a key reusable unit in the Wathba Skills system.

userStories.title: Implement the skill detail header and disclaimer treatment
userStories.description: Build the detail-page hero area with category badge, status badge, version, last verified metadata, title, summary, and warning notice for compliance skills.
acceptanceCriteria: The skill detail page shows category, status, version, and last verified badges at the top.
The page shows localized title and plain-language summary.
Skills with disclaimers render a warning notice prominently near the top.
The page includes a clear back-to-library action.
The header layout remains readable in English and Arabic.
userStories.notes: Compliance metadata must be impossible to miss.

userStories.title: Render skill detail previews, metadata panels, and sources
userStories.description: Finish the skill detail experience with the raw skill preview, variables panel, references count, scripts count, source list, maintainers, and version row.
acceptanceCriteria: The detail page includes a preview block for the skill body.
The page includes summary panels for variables, references, and scripts.
The page renders the skill's source links or source labels.
The page renders maintainer and version information.
The preview and metadata adapt correctly to RTL and narrow screens.
userStories.notes: This story turns the prototype detail layout into a production-grade browsing view.

userStories.title: Implement the recommendation engine from questionnaire answers
userStories.description: Translate the prototype's answer-to-skill logic into a reusable recommendation engine that suggests the right skills based on market, invoicing, PII, identity, payments, CI, and secrets answers.
acceptanceCriteria: KSA or GCC plus invoicing recommends zatca-phase2.
KSA or GCC plus PII recommends pdpl-basics.
KSA or GCC plus identity recommends nafath-yakeen-basics.
KSA or GCC plus payments recommends mada-stcpay-basics.
Secrets handling other than a proper manager recommends secrets-baseline.
Identity or PII recommends auth-isolation.
Missing CI recommends ci-hygiene.
Testability-check is always included.
Recommended skills are ordered saudi first, then security, then architecture.
userStories.notes: This logic is explicitly present in the prototype and should be preserved as the initial rules engine.

userStories.title: Build the four-step questionnaire shell and stepper
userStories.description: Implement the generator flow shell using the prototype's four-step structure and visible progress stepper.
acceptanceCriteria: The generate flow is split into About your project, Tech & agents, Review & variables, and Generate steps.
A stepper shows the current step and completed steps.
Back and continue actions behave predictably across steps.
The stepper works in both English and Arabic.
The flow is usable from keyboard alone.
userStories.notes: The questionnaire should feel like the prototype, not a generic long form.

userStories.title: Implement the 'About your project' step with KSA-aware branching
userStories.description: Build the first questionnaire step so market selection drives whether invoicing, payments, and identity questions appear, while PII remains relevant more broadly.
acceptanceCriteria: The first step asks for primary market.
If the selected market is KSA or GCC, invoicing, payments, and identity questions are shown.
If the selected market is global or other, the Saudi-specific follow-up questions are hidden.
The PII question is still asked when the market is global or other.
Each question can show a 'why we ask' explanation where the prototype provides one.
userStories.notes: This step captures the most important domain branching in the product.

userStories.title: Implement the 'Tech & agents' step
userStories.description: Build the second questionnaire step so users can specify stack, target agents, CI posture, and current secret handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can select a primary backend stack from the supported options.
Users can multi-select one or more target agents.
Users can answer whether CI runs on pull requests.
Users can choose how secrets are handled today.
All controls remain accessible and correctly localized.
userStories.notes: The available options should mirror the prototype's stack and agent taxonomy unless intentionally extended.

userStories.title: Add step-level validation and required-state handling
userStories.description: Prevent users from advancing with incomplete data by enforcing the prototype's conditional required fields and inline error presentation.
acceptanceCriteria: Market is required on the first step.
PII is required on the first step in all markets.
When market is KSA or GCC, invoicing, payments, and identity are required on the first step.
Stack, at least one agent, CI, and secrets are required on the second step.
Error feedback appears inline and clears when the field is corrected.
userStories.notes: Validation must respect branching rather than treating all fields as globally required.

userStories.title: Render the review step with auto-recommended skills
userStories.description: Build the review experience that lists recommended skills first, lets users inspect what was chosen for them, and prepares the selection state for generation.
acceptanceCriteria: The review step shows the recommended skills derived from the user's answers.
Each recommended skill row includes title, description, status badge, version, last verified date, and disclaimer marker when applicable.
Recommended rows are selected by default when first entering the step.
Users can toggle recommended rows on or off without losing the record of their recommendation source.
The review step has localized lede copy and labels.
userStories.notes: This story captures the prototype's conversion moment where recommendations become editable choices.

userStories.title: Implement the manual 'add another skill' drawer
userStories.description: Allow users to go beyond recommendations by expanding a manual picker of non-recommended skills and adding them to the current selection.
acceptanceCriteria: The review step contains an 'add another skill' control.
Expanding the control reveals non-recommended skills from the library.
Users can add or remove those skills from the active selection.
Manually added skills are visibly labeled differently from recommended ones.
The manual picker works in English and Arabic and on mobile.
userStories.notes: This is present in the prototype and important for expert users.

userStories.title: Model selected skills with source provenance
userStories.description: Keep track of whether a selected skill was recommended automatically or added manually so the UI and later analytics-free product logic can distinguish them.
acceptanceCriteria: Selection state stores whether a skill is on or off.
Selection state stores whether the skill came from an auto recommendation or manual addition.
Selection state can be restored from persisted answers.
Toggling a skill preserves its provenance unless intentionally changed.
The review UI consumes this state without special-case branching.
userStories.notes: The prototype uses selected[id] = { on, source }; the production app should keep an equivalent model.

userStories.title: Collect variable values for active selected skills
userStories.description: Build the review-step variable forms so active skills that require extra information can collect those values before generation.
acceptanceCriteria: Only active selected skills with variables render variable input forms.
Select variables render as select inputs with the declared options.
Boolean variables render as accessible toggle or yes/no controls.
Variable values are stored in a stable per-skill key structure.
Where useful, a skill can inherit defaults from earlier questionnaire answers such as stack.
userStories.notes: This story turns the prototype's varVals behavior into a real input layer for generation.

userStories.title: Build the generate-step file tree summary
userStories.description: Show users exactly what their zip will contain by grouping the generated file paths by selected target and surfacing file totals before download.
acceptanceCriteria: The generate step shows a zip summary card.
The summary card groups files by target and directory.
The summary shows total file count and selected skill count.
The summary updates when targets or selected skills change.
The summary remains readable in both locales and on mobile.
userStories.notes: This is a core trust-building surface from the prototype.

userStories.title: Implement target preview tabs and target-specific notes
userStories.description: Let users switch between Claude, Cursor, Codex, and generic previews so they can inspect how the same selected skill set will be rendered per agent.
acceptanceCriteria: The generate step shows one tab for each selected target agent.
Switching tabs updates the previewed file path and content.
Each target displays explanatory notes about how rendering works for that agent.
If the active target is no longer selected, the preview falls back to an available target.
Target labels remain clear and localized where appropriate.
userStories.notes: The prototype proves the UX; the production system must back it with real renderers.

userStories.title: Implement canonical markdown variable resolution
userStories.description: Resolve skill content templates into concrete rendered markdown using questionnaire answers and per-skill variables before adapters turn them into target-specific files.
acceptanceCriteria: Canonical skill bodies support variable placeholders defined by the schema.
Variable values are resolved from skill-specific inputs and relevant questionnaire defaults.
Missing required variable values are surfaced before download.
Rendered markdown is deterministic for the same inputs.
The resolver is reusable by all target adapters.
userStories.notes: This story turns the prototype's sample previews into real content generation.

userStories.title: Implement the Claude Code adapter
userStories.description: Render selected skills into Claude Code's expected .claude/skills folder structure while preserving references and helper scripts when available.
acceptanceCriteria: Each selected skill renders to its own .claude/skills/<slug>/ folder.
The adapter outputs a SKILL.md file for each skill.
Reference files are included under references/ when present.
Scripts are included under scripts/ when present.
The Claude preview in the generate step reflects the real adapter output.
userStories.notes: Claude is the highest-fidelity target in the prototype and should stay that way.

userStories.title: Implement the Cursor adapter
userStories.description: Render selected skills into Cursor's .cursor/rules format while clearly handling references or scripts that cannot execute in Cursor's rule model.
acceptanceCriteria: Each selected skill can render to a .cursor/rules/<slug>.mdc file.
Cursor output is derived from the same canonical rendered content as other targets.
Unsupported executable behavior is expressed as read-only guidance rather than being silently dropped.
The Cursor preview reflects the real adapter output.
Generated Cursor output remains readable and consistent across multiple selected skills.
userStories.notes: The prototype already promises Cursor output, so the PRD must make it explicit.

userStories.title: Implement the Codex adapter
userStories.description: Render the selected skill set into a project-level AGENTS.md format suitable for Codex or ChatGPT-style coding agents.
acceptanceCriteria: Codex output generates a single AGENTS.md file.
Selected skills are aggregated into clear sections inside that file.
Each section includes source metadata such as version and last verified date where appropriate.
The preview shown for Codex matches the actual generated output.
The adapter can handle multiple selected skills without ambiguous ordering.
userStories.notes: The prototype treats Codex as an AGENTS.md target; the implementation should formalize that behavior.

userStories.title: Implement the generic AGENTS.md adapter
userStories.description: Provide a generic AGENTS.md output for tools that do not have a dedicated adapter but still consume repository-level instructions.
acceptanceCriteria: Generic output generates a single AGENTS.md file.
Its content is distinct from Codex only where target-specific wording is needed.
The generic preview reflects the real adapter output.
The adapter can be selected independently of Codex.
The generated file remains portable across agent tools that read AGENTS.md.
userStories.notes: This story keeps the product useful beyond branded agents.

userStories.title: Build browser-side zip packaging and download
userStories.description: Generate the final downloadable archive entirely in the browser so users can download their selected targets without any backend service.
acceptanceCriteria: The browser assembles all selected target outputs into one zip file.
The zip filename follows a predictable project-skills-date style.
The download button enters a working state while the zip is being assembled.
The UI shows a completed state when the zip is ready.
No skill content or answers are sent to a remote service during packaging.
userStories.notes: The prototype fakes download state; this story makes it real.

userStories.title: Implement the bilingual compare canvas route
userStories.description: Build the side-by-side parity canvas used in the prototype so designers and reviewers can compare English/LTR and Arabic/RTL renderings of the same screen from a single data source.
acceptanceCriteria: The app has a compare view reachable from the main navigation.
The compare view can switch between landing, questionnaire, review, generate, and detail screens.
Each compare screen shows English/LTR and Arabic/RTL side by side.
Both frames are rendered from the same underlying data and component structure.
The compare view is useful for visual QA rather than just decorative.
userStories.notes: This is a concrete system-design element from the prototype and should remain part of the product workflow.

userStories.title: Implement the edit-mode tweaks panel
userStories.description: Carry over the prototype's internal tweaks panel so designers or maintainers can quickly switch language, theme, and primary swatch in edit mode without affecting normal users.
acceptanceCriteria: An edit-mode-only tweaks panel exists.
The panel can switch language, theme, and primary swatch.
The panel can collapse and expand.
The panel communicates with the host or app state without breaking normal navigation.
When edit mode is inactive, the panel is hidden from regular users.
userStories.notes: This story is primarily for design iteration, but it is part of the prototype system design.

userStories.title: Create complete English and Arabic message catalogs
userStories.description: Move the prototype's bilingual copy into structured locale files so every screen, label, hint, and status string has a production-ready translation source.
acceptanceCriteria: All user-facing UI strings live in structured English and Arabic locale files.
Landing, library, detail, questionnaire, review, generate, compare, and footer copy are covered.
Status labels, action labels, and helper text are localized.
There is no hard-coded English-only UI text left in the main product flow.
Locale files are organized so contributors can add more languages later without rewriting components.
userStories.notes: The prototype already contains near-complete bilingual copy and should be treated as the baseline.

userStories.title: Meet the accessibility bar across the core flows
userStories.description: Make the product fully keyboard navigable and screen-reader friendly across landing, questionnaire, library, detail, review, and generate screens.
acceptanceCriteria: All interactive controls are reachable and usable by keyboard alone.
Custom radio-card, checkbox-card, toggle, and stepper interactions expose appropriate semantics.
Visible focus states exist for all interactive controls.
There are no keyboard traps in the questionnaire, compare view, or previews.
The main flows are screen-reader navigable with meaningful labels and headings.
userStories.notes: Accessibility is a core product requirement, not a later polish pass.

userStories.title: Verify RTL and bilingual visual parity
userStories.description: Systematically validate that Arabic RTL layouts are first-class across navigation, forms, cards, code previews, and detail metadata layouts.
acceptanceCriteria: All core screens are tested in both English and Arabic.
RTL flipping works for spacing, alignment, icon placement, and navigation direction.
Typography changes appropriately for Arabic headings and body copy.
The compare canvas helps reviewers detect parity regressions quickly.
Any component added to the system is considered incomplete until it has been checked in both directions.
userStories.notes: This story operationalizes the prototype's compare route as a quality discipline.

userStories.title: Add automated tests for logic, state, and rendering primitives
userStories.description: Protect the product's recommendation logic, state restoration, and rendering helpers with unit and component-level tests.
acceptanceCriteria: The recommendation engine has test coverage for its major branching rules.
State restoration from localStorage has test coverage for valid and malformed values.
Variable resolution logic has test coverage.
At least key UI primitives or page-level components have component tests.
Test failures block CI.
userStories.notes: The prototype logic is simple enough to test exhaustively; the production system should do so.

userStories.title: Add end-to-end coverage for questionnaire to download
userStories.description: Test the main value path from answering questions to downloading a zip so regressions in generation, routing, or state handling are caught early.
acceptanceCriteria: An end-to-end test covers landing to questionnaire entry.
The test fills the questionnaire, reaches review, and selects or confirms skills.
The test reaches the generate step and triggers download.
The test verifies the resulting file list or archive structure for at least one multi-target path.
At least one end-to-end scenario exercises Arabic or RTL behavior.
userStories.notes: The acceptance flow in the prototype should become the first real E2E path.

userStories.title: Run CI quality gates on every pull request
userStories.description: Automate validation for linting, typechecking, testing, skill generation, and build so the repo remains healthy as content and features expand.
acceptanceCriteria: A GitHub Actions workflow runs on pull requests.
CI installs dependencies with pnpm.
CI runs skill generation before dependent checks.
CI runs lint, typecheck, tests, and build.
Build or generation failures prevent merges.
userStories.notes: This story turns local discipline into enforced repository policy.

userStories.title: Ship the open-source governance and contributor documents
userStories.description: Complete the public project surface with README, CONTRIBUTING, DISCLAIMER, CODEOWNERS, issue templates, and license files that match Wathba Skills' content-first open-source model.
acceptanceCriteria: The repository includes an MIT license.
The repository includes a clear disclaimer document linked from the product.
The repository includes bilingual contribution guidance.
CODEOWNERS routes Saudi compliance, security, and web changes to the right maintainers.
README explains the product, repository structure, local development commands, and content contribution model.
userStories.notes: Open-source trust is part of the product, especially for compliance-oriented content.
